title: Darjeeling toy train, tea and Tiger Hill in three nights
summary: A short, easy Darjeeling break: three nights in town with a Tiger Hill sunrise, the toy train joy ride to Ghum, a tea garden walk, the zoo and HMI, and Kurseong on the way down. It suits a first visit, families and long weekends.
meta_description: Three nights in Darjeeling: Tiger Hill sunrise, steam toy train to Ghum, Happy Valley tea, zoo and HMI, Kurseong. Budget, Value and Comfort prices from NJP.
intro: This is the classic first visit to Darjeeling, built around the things most people come for: the toy train, the tea and the view of Kangchenjunga. Three nights in one hotel keep it relaxed, with no packing and unpacking, and leave a spare morning in case cloud spoils the first sunrise.

We drive up from NJP or Bagdogra rather than taking the full 7–8 hour train, then ride the best section of the railway on the joy ride from Darjeeling to Ghum. On the way down we stop in Kurseong for Makaibari tea and the train in the bazaar.
highlights: A steam or diesel joy ride on the UNESCO-listed Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, with stops at the Batasia Loop and Ghum.
Sunrise on Kangchenjunga from Tiger Hill, with Everest on the clearest mornings.
A walk and tasting at Happy Valley, founded in 1854 and only 3 km from town.
Red pandas and snow leopards at the Himalayan zoo, and Tenzing Norgay's story at HMI.
Tea and the toy train in the bazaar at Kurseong on the drive back down.

days.title: NJP or Bagdogra to Darjeeling
days.text: Meet your car or join a shared jeep at NJP or Bagdogra and climb through Sukna's forest, the Rohini tea gardens, Kurseong and Ghum to Darjeeling at about 2,045 m. Check in, rest for an hour to let your body adjust, then walk up to Chowrasta in the late afternoon. Stroll the Mall loop around Observatory Hill and have an early dinner, as tomorrow starts before dawn.

days.title: Tiger Hill sunrise and the toy train to Ghum
days.drive: 25 km in total, about 4 hours with stops
days.text: Leave at about 4 am for Tiger Hill and watch first light on Kangchenjunga. On the way back stop at Ghum Monastery and the Batasia Loop. After breakfast and a rest, take the late-morning or afternoon toy train joy ride from Darjeeling to Ghum and back, about two hours, with a halt at Batasia and time at the Ghum railway museum. Evening free around Chowrasta.

days.title: Tea garden, zoo and HMI
days.text: Walk down to Happy Valley Tea Estate for a garden visit and tasting, then take a taxi to the Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park and the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute next door (closed on Thursdays). After lunch, visit the Tibetan Refugee Self-Help Centre or the Japanese Peace Pagoda. End with tea and cake at Glenary's on Nehru Road. Pick up tea to take home from an estate outlet rather than a roadside stall.

days.title: Darjeeling to Kurseong and down to NJP
days.text: Drive down to Kurseong, about 1–1.5 hours. Visit Makaibari Tea Estate for a walk and tasting, then watch the toy train pass through Kurseong bazaar if timings work. Take the Rohini or Pankhabari road down to the plains and reach NJP or Bagdogra by mid-afternoon, in time for evening trains and flights. Keep a buffer for slow traffic near Siliguri.

Breakfast and dinner on days 2 and 3, breakfast on day 4, dinner on day 1
Transfers and sightseeing by shared jeep (Budget) or private car (Value and Comfort)
Toy train joy ride ticket (diesel for Budget, steam for Value and Comfort)
Tiger Hill trip and three-point sightseeing
excludes: Flights and trains to NJP or Bagdogra
Entry fees for the zoo, HMI, Tiger Hill gallery and tea tastings
good_to_know: Toy train joy ride seats sell out weeks ahead in October and May; we book as soon as you confirm.
If Tiger Hill is clouded on day 2, we move the sunrise trip to day 3 or day 4.
The zoo and HMI close on Thursdays, so we swap days 2 and 3 if needed.
Darjeeling lanes are steep and cars cannot reach every hotel; pack in a bag you can carry a short way.
Prices are indicative for 2025–26 and rise around Durga Puja, Diwali and Christmas.

save_tips: Travel in November, February or early April for lower hotel rates and clear weather.
Take shared jeeps between NJP and Darjeeling instead of a reserved car to save ₹2,500–3,000.
Choose the diesel joy ride, which covers the same route and stops as steam for a lower fare.
Eat in Tibetan and Nepali cafés around Chowrasta and Chowk Bazar rather than hotel restaurants.
Walk to Happy Valley and the zoo instead of hiring a taxi for each sight.

faqs.q: Is three nights enough for Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Three nights is enough for the main sights at an easy pace: Tiger Hill, Ghum and Batasia, the toy train, a tea garden, the zoo and HMI, and the town itself. It also leaves a spare morning if the first sunrise is cloudy. If you want Mirik, Sandakphu or a tea-estate stay, add two or more nights.

faqs.q: Why not take the toy train all the way from NJP?
faqs.a: The full NJP to Darjeeling train takes 7–8 hours to cover 88 km, which uses a whole day of a short trip. The joy ride from Darjeeling to Ghum gives you the most famous section, the Batasia Loop and the railway museum in two hours. If you love trains and have a spare day, we can add the full journey.

faqs.q: Steam or diesel for the joy ride?
faqs.a: Steam is the real thing, with vintage British-built engines, smoke and whistles, and we include it in the Value and Comfort tiers. Diesel covers the same route and stops for less and is included in the Budget tier. You can upgrade Budget to steam for the fare difference, about ₹400–700 per person, if seats are available.

faqs.q: What is the best month for this trip?
faqs.a: October and November give the clearest views, followed by March to May and the cold, bright months of December to February. Avoid the monsoon from June to September, when Tiger Hill is usually clouded and landslides can disrupt the roads and toy train. If you travel in October, book at least six weeks ahead.

faqs.q: Is this trip suitable for children and elderly travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Drives are short, the pace is easy and there is no trekking. The Tiger Hill start at 4 am is optional for anyone who prefers to sleep. Darjeeling's lanes are steep, so for older travellers we choose a hotel with car access in the Value and Comfort tiers. Pack warm clothes even in spring.

faqs.q: How much does the Budget tier cost and what does it include?
faqs.a: From about ₹9,500 per person, twin sharing, for three nights in a family guesthouse, most meals, shared jeeps, the Tiger Hill trip and a diesel joy ride. Entry fees, lunches and tips are extra. Prices are indicative for 2025–26 and rise in peak weeks. Solo travellers pay a single supplement of about ₹2,500–3,500.

faqs.q: Can I start from Bagdogra instead of NJP?
faqs.a: Yes. Bagdogra airport is about 3 hours from Darjeeling, similar to NJP. For day 1, choose a flight landing before about 1 pm so you reach Darjeeling in daylight. On day 4 we aim to reach Bagdogra by about 2 pm; book an afternoon or evening flight to allow for slow mountain traffic.

faqs.q: What if the toy train is cancelled?
faqs.a: Joy rides are occasionally cancelled for engine faults, landslides or special events. IRCTC refunds the fare for cancelled trains. We then add an alternative such as the Batasia Loop and Ghum museum by car, or rebook for another day of your stay if seats are free. Check current status before you travel in the monsoon.

faqs.q: Can I add Mirik or Kalimpong to this trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Add one night in Mirik on day 4 and return to NJP on day 5 via a different road, or add a night in Kalimpong, about 2.5 hours from Darjeeling. Each extra night adds roughly ₹2,500–4,000 per person in the Budget tier and more in the Value and Comfort tiers, depending on the hotel.
